note: The skill path of every career the product lists, and the only place the paths are decided. Each career of data/careers/catalogue.json has one entry, by `title`, with its `skills` by their exact names in data/skills/catalogue.json. A path names skills and sets no level: each skill sits at its own level (data/skills/taxonomy.json), and the taxonomy orders them on screen. They are listed here Fundamentals first for reading only. `basis` says in a sentence or two where the path was read from. A skill written as { skill, why } is one a reader might question. `lacks` names what the job needs that the catalogue has no skill for; it is a list for whoever next works on the catalogue and is not loaded. `weakLinks` are the ladder links of the careers catalogue across which less than a third of the lower career's skills carry: each is acknowledged here with its reason, and the check fails on one that is not. scripts/build-career-paths-sql.mjs validates this file (--check) and generates the migration that loads it; a path a person has approved is never changed by it.

careers.title: Production Operator
careers.basis: The entry job of most plants. Of 38 production operator and technician postings read, 31 ask work to written instructions, 26 name safety, 15 calipers, 14 a forklift and 12 the plant system or lot records; lockout and the control chart are named by almost none and are here because an operator is trained in both before running alone. The catalogue note says there is no trade skill in this job.

skills.why: Named in 1 of 38 postings, required of every machine operator by the plant before the posting is ever read.
Operators feed their own line in most plants: named in 14 of 38 operator postings.
The operator's part of it: plot the measurement, stop on an out-of-control point. Named in 2 of 38 postings; kept because the operator is the one at the chart.

careers.title: Setup Technician
careers.basis: Written around the changeover, as the catalogue note asks: the operator's floor skills kept, then the mold or die change, first-article approval and the upkeep a setter does on the way to maintenance. CNC set-up is CNC Machinist's.

skills.why: The stamping version of the same job.
The plastics version of the changeover; plastics plants are where this career is most listed.
Clamps, ejectors and feeders are air; a setter fixes the leak or the cylinder that stops a changeover.

careers.title: Continuous Improvement Specialist
careers.basis: The lean toolkit in the order a plant teaches it: 5S and standard work, then mapping, timing and loss data, then leading events and belt projects. From the career description and the present path; only four postings carried the title, so postings add nothing here.

careers.title: Industrial Engineer
careers.basis: Everything the improvement specialist uses, plus the engineering side: layouts drawn in CAD and the statistics behind a capacity claim. Of 26 industrial engineering and continuous improvement postings read (Anduril 16), 14 name layout, 13 time studies or cycle time, 12 simulation and 10 line balancing; O*NET 17-2112 tasks say the same (layouts, statistical methods, standards).

skills.why: Plant and cell layouts are drawn in 2D.

careers.title: CNC Machine Operator
careers.basis: Kept to operating, offsets and in-process measurement, as the catalogue note asks. Relativity's CNC Machine Operator I posting ("set up and operate CNC machines with FANUC controls", work and tool offsets, first-piece and in-process inspection) and the federal Machining standard as the sources report quotes it (Machine Tool Operator grade 8: jobs "set up in the machine ... by a higher grade worker") draw the same line. The hand gauges are in O*NET's tools list for machinists (dial indicators, pin gauge sets, deburring tools).

skills.why: An operator runs both machine types from a setup sheet; choosing the workholding and proving the program is the next rung.

careers.title: CNC Machinist
careers.basis: The operator's path plus what makes a set-up person. Of 43 machinist postings read (SpaceX 22, RTX, Northrop, Relativity, John Deere), 33 ask set-up, 35 tooling, 20 fixtures or workholding, 19 GD&T, 15 editing programs, 15 mill-turn or multi-axis lathes, 12 five-axis and 10 manual machines. In the federal standard Machinist grade 10 sets up "most types of conventional and CNC machine tools" and grade 11 adds "debugging first run programs". Feeds and speeds, probing and first article are named by few postings and come from the apprenticeship framework and the trade.

skills.why: Manual machines are named in 10 of 43 machinist postings (RTX asks two years on them); the catalogue note keeps them here.
Named in 4 of 43 postings; kept because a set-up on a current machine is probed, and the catalogue added it for this career.
Reading and editing at the control, not writing from the model: that is the programmer.

careers.title: Swiss CNC Machinist
careers.basis: A CNC machinist who has moved to the sliding-headstock lathe: the turning side of the trade kept, the mill side dropped, and what small long-run parts add (comparator, thread gauging, charts over a long run).

skills.why: A Swiss machine is a live-tool, sub-spindle lathe; this is its Advanced end.

careers.title: CNC Programmer
careers.basis: The machinist's set-up knowledge carried into the office: CAM from the model, the tool list, simulation before the machine, the fixture the job is planned around. Of 10 programmer postings read (SpaceX, Northrop, Anduril), all name tooling, 8 CAM software, 6 fixtures and 6 five-axis or multi-axis work; the catalogue note names the same skills.

skills.why: Programs are made from the released model and kept under revision with it. Named in 1 of 10 postings; my judgment.
The folded title NC Fixture Programmer: the programmer designs the soft jaws and fixtures a job needs.

careers.title: Precision Grinder
careers.basis: Grinding to tenths is measuring to tenths: the trade's own four skills with the bench metrology that proves them. O*NET 51-4033 tasks (set up and tend grinding, lapping and honing machines; measure with micrometers); no posting carried the title.

careers.title: EDM Operator
careers.basis: Both machines, with the set-up and the checks a die detail needs. From the career description and the present path; the one EDM posting read is a programmer's. Nothing in the catalogue is Advanced for this trade: its next step is the toolmaker.

skills.why: Die openings and wire-cut slots are checked with pins.
Sinker electrodes are milled by the person who burns with them.

careers.title: Tool and Die Maker
careers.basis: The apprenticeship in one path: machine the details (mill, lathe, grind, EDM), fit them, then spot and try the die out. The federal Toolmaking standard (grade 13: "planning, layout, machining, assembly, and hand finishing" of jigs, fixtures, gauges, punches, dies and molds) and O*NET 51-4111, whose tools list has gauge blocks, die spotting presses and EDM and wire EDM machines.

skills.why: The folded title Gage Maker.

careers.title: Jig and Fixture Builder
careers.basis: Rewritten toward building and setting tooling, as the catalogue note asks: a fabricator's welding and fit-up, a toolroom's machining and bench metrology, and the tracker that certifies a large tool to its datums. Of 7 tooling technician and toolmaker postings read (SpaceX 4, Anduril, GM, Saronic), 6 name machining, 4 welding and 4 a laser tracker.

skills.why: A fixture is built to a share of the part tolerance; the builder works out what the locators may use.
How assembly jigs and layup tools are set and certified.

careers.title: MIG Welder
careers.basis: The first rung of the welding trade: one wire process learned well, with fit-up, cutting and the eye for a good weld. Of 54 welder postings read, 50 ask a welding certification or test, 43 drawings or weld symbols, 33 a crane or hoist and 21 MIG by name; O*NET 51-4121 tools include MIG welders, cutting torches and fillet weld gauges.

skills.why: A welder moves the weldment: 33 of 54 welder postings name cranes or hoists.
Even a first welding job is hired on a bend test to a code.

careers.title: Welder
careers.basis: The MIG welder's path plus the other arc processes and positions. Of 54 welder postings read, 35 name TIG, 29 stainless, 28 pipe or tube, 24 aluminum, 15 flux-cored and 14 stick; the catalogue note brings the qualification and bend-test skills from Certified Welder.

careers.title: TIG Welder
careers.basis: Precision manual welding on thin and reactive metal. The 10 TIG welder postings read are all SpaceX's and ask welding of stainless, Inconel, aluminum or titanium, tube included; 21 of 54 welder postings name AWS D17.1. Orbital welding (2 of 54) and brazing (5 of 54) are named by few and are here as the directions the trade specialises in.

skills.why: Tube and fitting shops braze with the same torch hand. Named beside TIG in 5 of 54 welder postings.

careers.title: Aerospace Welder
careers.basis: The TIG welder on flight hardware: tanks, pressure vessels and tube in aluminum-lithium, stainless and titanium, on clean joints. The folded titles are all tank and vessel work and the catalogue note lists the path; 14 of 54 welder postings ask welds to X-ray quality.

skills.why: How tank barrels and domes are seamed today; the welder runs the machine as well as the torch.
Weld joints and tube for propellant service are cleaned before and after welding.

careers.title: Robotic Welding Technician
careers.basis: A welder who tends the cell: knows a good weld by hand, then touches up points on the pendant, keeps torch, tip and liner right and cuts and etches samples. Three postings carried the title (SpaceX 2, Panasonic 1), all asking robot programming or pendant work and maintenance; the rest is from the career description and the skill added last round.

skills.why: The torch is the tool: its centre point is reset after every crash or neck change.

careers.title: Laser Welding Technician
careers.basis: Laser joining is a process job more than a hand skill: set-up, seam checks by section, optics and the process window. From the career description and the present path, with the optics skill added last round.

skills.why: The other beam process, set up and proven the same way; no career in the catalogue is closer to it.

careers.title: Body Weld Technician
careers.basis: One body shop, every joining station: spot, rivet and screw, adhesive, hem, the MIG and braze repairs, and the teardown that proves the welds. The catalogue note folds nineteen station titles here. No body shop technician posting was among those read, so this rests on the note and the trade.

skills.why: Weld guns and their caps are the robot's tooling; changing and re-teaching them is daily work.

careers.title: Sheet Metal Fabricator
careers.basis: Flat pattern to finished enclosure: layout, cut, brake, join. The federal Sheet Metal Mechanic standard (grade 10 "develop patterns and lay out, cut, form, join, assemble") and O*NET 47-2211 tools; six postings carried the title, most of them aircraft sheet metal.

skills.why: The one Advanced sheet skill in the catalogue: domes and cones a brake cannot make.

careers.title: Metal Fabricator
careers.basis: The fitter-welder: cut, fit and weld plate and structural shapes square and to size, and move the weldment. O*NET 51-2041 tasks ("position, align, fit, and weld parts", tack welding, checking with squares and rules); the welder's processes are kept so the ladder from Welder shows.

skills.why: Where plate fabrication specialises: vessels and tanks built to a code.

careers.title: Laser Cutting Operator
careers.basis: Three cutting tables in one career, differing by one skill each (the catalogue note), with the material handling a table operator does alone.

careers.title: Stamping Press Operator
careers.basis: Runs the press and reads the panel. Setting the die and cutting changeover time are the next rung's, so they are taken off this path.

careers.title: Die Setter
careers.basis: The press operator who changes the die: crane and rigging, shut height and feed, first hits approved, and the changeover made shorter. The catalogue note lists these additions; die spotting and tryout belong to the die maker and are taken off.

careers.title: Die Maintenance Technician
careers.basis: Between the press and the toolroom: pulls a die, replaces and fits worn details, welds and regrinds damage, spots it back in and proves it. Stamping and casting dies both, since both rungs below lead here.

skills.why: Die steel is repaired by weld build-up before it is reground.
The panel is how a die tells what is wrong with it.

skills: Die Casting Die Setup and Maintenance

careers.title: Die Casting Machine Operator
careers.basis: The cell through its cycle, with the melt, the trim and the X-ray check the folded titles bring. Shot and vacuum settings are the technician's.

careers.title: Die Casting Technician
careers.basis: Sets the cell up and keeps it in process: die change, shot, vacuum and spray, and the defect traced to its cause. From the draft path of Die Cast Setup Technician, with the operator's skills kept under it.
skills: Die Casting Die Setup and Maintenance

careers.title: Casting Process Engineer
careers.basis: Owns the process windows the technician sets, and proves them: trials, X-ray and section results, scrap by cause. Sand and investment casting were added to the catalogue last round for this career.

skills.why: The other two foundry processes; a casting engineer is hired for one and expected to know all three.
Porosity and microstructure are read from a section.

careers.title: Injection Molding Operator
careers.basis: An operator's floor skills around the one trade skill the catalogue now has for the press. Mold changes are the setup technician's.
lacks: material drying and handling as its own skill

careers.title: Additive Manufacturing Technician
careers.basis: Powder in, part out: build preparation, the printer, then stress relief, cutting from the plate and finishing. Of 5 additive technician postings read (Relativity 3, Anduril, SpaceX), 4 name powder, 4 post-processing, 3 respirators or protective equipment and 2 EDM.

skills.why: Reactive powder is handled in a respirator.
How metal parts leave the build plate.

careers.title: Additive Manufacturing Engineer
careers.basis: The technician's process knowledge plus design for the process and the qualification behind a printed part: parameters by experiment, density by CT and section, properties by tensile bar.

careers.title: Laser Technician
careers.basis: A service technician for laser systems: the uses the catalogue describes (cutting, welding, marking), the beam path, the chiller and the electrical fault-finding. Short, because the trade's own work is one skill.
lacks: resonator and beam-delivery alignment as more than upkeep

careers.title: Heat Treat Operator
careers.basis: The furnace cycles a commercial heat treater runs, steel and aluminum, with the hardness check that releases the load and the records that go with it. O*NET 51-4191 tasks (set furnace temperatures and times from work orders, record that parts reached them); vacuum, nitriding and pyrometry are the specialisations an accredited shop adds. One posting carried the title.

skills.why: Baskets and fixtures go in and out of the furnace and the quench on a hoist.
Brazing in a vacuum or atmosphere furnace is run by the heat treat shop, on its furnaces.

careers.title: Plating and Anodizing Technician
careers.basis: One tank line, every process on it, with the chemical handling a plating shop is built around. O*NET 51-4193 tasks (mix and test solutions, measure deposit thickness); the catalogue note folds five single-process titles here. No posting carried the title.

skills.why: Parts are masked before the tank exactly as before the booth; the catalogue has one masking skill.

careers.title: Thermal Spray Technician
careers.basis: Mask, blast, spray, prove: the two trade skills added last round with the preparation and the coating checks around them. No posting carried the title and the employers read do little of this work; O*NET 51-9124 lists thermal spray systems among a coater's tools, and the rest is from the trade itself.

skills.why: Production spray guns and peening nozzles are robot-carried.
A sprayed coating is accepted on the section of a test coupon.

careers.title: Industrial Painter
careers.basis: Prepare, mask, coat by liquid or powder, cure, check film and finish. O*NET 51-9124 tasks and tools (spray guns, HVLP systems); powder coating was added last round for this career. The six painter postings read name none of the skills in a way that could be counted.

careers.title: Aircraft Painter
careers.basis: The industrial painter's hand skills on an airframe: stripped and conversion-coated before primer, painted from a lift, to an aerospace specification. The catalogue note brings low-observable coating as the Advanced end.

skills.why: An aircraft is painted from lifts and stands, in a harness.

careers.title: Automotive Paint Technician
careers.basis: One paint shop from bare body to finished colour: the twenty-four stations the catalogue note folds here make exactly these skills.

careers.title: Paint Process Engineer
careers.basis: Owns what the paint technician runs: bath chemistry, robot application, film build and appearance, and the statistics and problem solving of an engineer. From the career description; the eight paint engineer postings read are mostly a rocket maker's (paint and thermal protection) and name none of a vehicle paint shop's processes.

careers.title: Composite Technician
careers.basis: Kit, lay up, bag, cure, trim. Of 20 composite technician postings read (Rocket Lab 8, Anduril, Northrop, SpaceX), 17 name oven cure, 11 autoclave, 12 bonding, 12 infusion or resin transfer, 10 bagging, 7 layup and 7 prepreg; the federal Composite/Plastic Fabricating standard grades the same work from surface repair up to one-of-a-kind fabrication. Ultrasonic testing and scarf repair are taken off as the catalogue note asks.

skills.why: Prepreg out-time and lot are recorded ply by ply.
The wound-part version of layup: pressure vessels and tubes.
Bonding is named in 12 of 20 composite technician postings; the rest of the bonding skills stay with the bonding technician.

careers.title: Automated Fiber Placement Operator
careers.basis: A composite technician at a CNC placement machine: the hand skills are kept for the repairs between courses, and every ply is inspected.

skills.why: The placement machine is run from a CNC control like any machine tool.

careers.title: Autoclave Operator
careers.basis: Load, instrument, run and release the cure. The draft path, with the layup shop's bagging and thermocouple skills under it.

careers.title: Composite Bonding Technician
careers.basis: A bond is its surface preparation: prep, adhesive, core and details, bag and cure, then the tap check. From the draft path and the catalogue note (honeycomb core).

careers.title: Composite Repair Technician
careers.basis: Layup and bonding turned to repair: both lower rungs' skills are kept, with the repair manual, drying, the scarf and the damage call added. The federal standard 4352 grades composite repair from surface damage (grade 7) to structure whose contour and strength must be restored (9 and 10).

careers.title: Materials Testing Technician
careers.basis: The mechanical and metallurgical laboratory: hardness, tensile, alloy identification, sections, and the report against the specification. The catalogue note lists the path; positive material identification was added last round.

skills.why: How an aluminum temper is checked without cutting the part.

careers.title: Materials Engineer
careers.basis: The laboratory's tests read with authority: the engineer sets the heat treatment and weld procedure, qualifies them, and decides what happens to material that fails. Of 29 materials engineer postings read (SpaceX 21), 24 name specifications, 14 failure analysis, 13 metallography, 11 mechanical testing, 11 welding and 7 heat treatment; the review board is named by 4 and is here from the career description.

skills.why: Materials and processes engineers own the special-process specifications, welding first among them.

careers.title: Production Assembler
careers.basis: The entry job of an assembly floor. Of 24 assembler postings read, 20 name the plant system or a traveler, 18 work to instructions, 13 hand and power tools, 13 drawings, 9 measuring and 8 inspecting their own work; O*NET 51-2092 lists torque wrenches and torque drivers. Nothing here is Advanced.

careers.title: Precision Assembly Technician
careers.basis: The assembler who builds from the drawing and measures as the build goes: fits, bearings, shims and the rework when a stack-up does not close. The additions are the catalogue note's. The 18 mechanical assembly technician postings read say little beyond drawings (10) and torque (5), so the fitting skills rest on the note and the trade.

skills.why: Filed under airframe assembly in the catalogue, but it is how any precision stack-up is closed.

careers.title: Machine Builder
careers.basis: A machine-tool builder's floor, as the catalogue note describes it: castings rigged into place, guides, screws and spindle fitted, then the geometry scraped, aligned, measured and compensated. The catalogue's machine tool building group is this career.

skills.why: Lubrication, coolant, hydraulic and air lines are plumbed during the build.

careers.title: Automotive Assembler
careers.basis: General assembly, station by station: the thirty-three line titles the catalogue note folds here are these seven installations, done to takt and torque. Vehicle plants post this job without naming a skill (nine production associate postings read, none naming a tool), so the path is the catalogue's vehicle final assembly group.

skills.why: A line station is worked to its standard work sheet and takt time.

careers.title: Body Fit Technician
careers.basis: Closures hung, gaps and flush set, the dings picked out before paint. The catalogue has few skills for this station, so the path is short; metal finishing was added last round.

skills.why: A fit problem is often a panel problem: the fitter stones and checks the panel first.

careers.title: Powertrain Assembler
careers.basis: Engines, gearboxes and drive units: the two build skills added last round, on the draft path of Drive Unit Assembler (bearings, press fits, housing), with the leak and electrical checks each unit passes.

skills.why: Every drive unit is high-potential tested before it leaves the cell.

careers.title: Aircraft Structures Mechanic
careers.basis: Drill, deburr, seal, fasten, shim, join. Of 20 structures mechanic and technician postings read (Lockheed 6, SpaceX 6, Relativity 4, Boeing 2), 13 name drilling or reaming, 10 sealant, 9 rivets, 9 deburring, 9 conversion coating touch-up, 8 shims and 5 cold working; O*NET 51-2011 lists rivet guns, bucking bars and reamers; the federal Sheet Metal Mechanic standard puts airframes and control surfaces at grade 10.

skills.why: Bare aluminum is touched up after drilling and trimming: named in 9 of 20 structures postings.
The folded title Structural Repair Mechanic; repair is where the federal standard puts the top of this trade.

careers.title: Aircraft Systems Mechanic
careers.basis: What goes inside the structure: tubes and hoses, controls, gear, then each system leak-checked, rigged and closed out. The catalogue note lists the path; a structures mechanic brings the airframe habits and bracket-fastening skills, and leaves the riveting behind.

skills.why: Tubes, tanks and components are bonded to structure as they are installed.

careers.title: Rocket Engine Technician
careers.basis: Clean assembly of a liquid engine, joint by joint. Of 29 engine build and propulsion technician postings read (SpaceX 21, Relativity, Rocket Lab), 20 name proof or pressure testing, 14 cranes or hoists, 13 valves, 9 fittings and tubing and 7 each torque, leak checks, cleanliness and brazing; safety wire and borescope are named by 2 each and are here from the present path. The four Advanced skills are the component specialisations the folded titles name.

skills.why: Engines and their modules are moved on hoists: 14 of 29 postings.
Named in 7 of 29 engine build postings; chambers, injectors and tube joints are brazed.
Turbopump and valve builds turn on bearing fits.
A chamber shop skill kept here because the engine technician's folded titles include chamber and nozzle builders.

careers.title: Propulsion Technician
careers.basis: The engine technician's fluid skills on the vehicle: tanks, bottles, valves, tube runs and thrusters installed and proven leak-tight. The installations are the catalogue note's. Of 64 fluids, propulsion and integration technician postings read, 17 name leak or proof testing and 11 tube bending or fabrication.

skills.why: Vehicle tube runs are welded in place. Named in 4 of 64 postings; here from the catalogue note.

careers.title: Launch Vehicle Integration Technician
careers.basis: Stages are large structure moved by crane and joined at height: lifting and rigging, the join, the mechanisms, the heat shield, and the inspection of what comes back. The catalogue note lists the path; the isogrid machining and tank welding on the present path belong to other trades.

careers.title: Spacecraft Integration Technician
careers.basis: Assembly, integration and test of a satellite: structure and units, harness, blankets, mechanisms, then support through test. Of 9 satellite technician postings read (SpaceX 8), all name mechanical work and test, 7 electrical or harness work and 7 thermal vacuum or vibration; the installations are from the catalogue note.
lacks: solar array installation and deployment test
spacecraft lifting and handling in ground support equipment

careers.title: Missile and Ordnance Technician
careers.basis: Two trade skills and the shared assembly, harness and test skills around them, as the catalogue note says. Nothing here is Advanced because the catalogue has nothing Advanced for the trade.
lacks: explosive safety beyond handling (site quantity-distance, grounding systems)

careers.title: Medical Device Assembler
careers.basis: The regulated-room skills only: the catalogue has nothing device-specific, so this is the honest short path. From the catalogue note; no device maker's postings were read.
lacks: catheter bonding, tipping and UV adhesive work

careers.title: Electronics Assembler
careers.basis: Hand soldering to IPC, then the unit built up in its enclosure. Seven electronics assembly postings carried the title: all name soldering, 5 electromechanical or chassis assembly, 4 J-STD-001 and 4 ESD control; O*NET 51-2022 tools are soldering irons, wire crimpers and pin extractors.

skills.why: The certification the trade names as its step up; the catalogue keeps it as a skill for that reason.

careers.title: SMT Line Operator
careers.basis: One line, machine by machine: print, inspect paste, place, reflow, inspect, then wave, depanel and coat. The eight machine titles the catalogue note folds here are these skills; the programming of each machine is the Advanced end.

careers.title: PCB Rework Technician
careers.basis: Where hand soldering becomes a specialisation: fine-pitch and BGA removal and replacement, proven by X-ray. Leans Advanced because the work is.

skills.why: A BGA site is re-pasted through a mini-stencil before the part goes back.
Coating is stripped for the repair and put back after it.

careers.title: Electronics Technician
careers.basis: Schematic, meter and scope down to the failed part, and prototypes built for engineers. Of 13 electrical engineering and electronics technician postings read (Anduril 10), 12 name troubleshooting, 12 harness or cable work, 11 schematics, 9 an oscilloscope, 8 a multimeter and 6 each soldering and rework; the federal Electronics Mechanic standard grades the same work from subassemblies (grade 8) to whole systems (11).

careers.title: Wire Harness Assembler
careers.basis: Cut, strip, crimp, pin, lace, test: the cable and harness group of the catalogue is this career. Five harness postings carried the title; all name lacing or tying and coaxial work, 3 crimping and 3 the IPC/WHMA-A-620 standard.

careers.title: Electrical Panel Builder
careers.basis: A panel from its drawings: layout, drill and mount, wire, ferrule, label, test. Control panel building was added last round for this career; the catalogue note lists the rest. Nothing in the catalogue is Advanced for it.

skills.why: Back panels and enclosures are laid out, drilled and tapped before a wire is run.

careers.title: Aircraft Electrician
careers.basis: The harness builder's skills carried onto the aircraft: route and clamp, terminate, bond and ground, ring out, close out. The catalogue note lists the additions.

careers.title: Avionics Technician
careers.basis: Installs the boxes and proves the systems. Of 20 avionics technician postings read (SpaceX 12, Rocket Lab 4, Relativity 3), 17 name harness work, 13 soldering, 12 troubleshooting and 10 each connectors and functional test; none names a data bus, so the four Advanced skills are from the thirty-three folded titles, each one box or bus.

skills.why: Line-replaceable units are loaded with their software on the aircraft.

careers.title: Power Electronics Technician
careers.basis: Module to inverter: die attach and bonding, then busbars, thermal interface, cooling and potting, then the high-voltage tests. The draft path of Power Module Technician with the three skills the catalogue note brings.
skills: Cold Plate and Coolant Loop Assembly

careers.title: Server Assembly Technician
careers.basis: Build sheet to burn-in: components, cooling, rack and cabling, firmware and image. The catalogue's server integration group is this career; nothing in it is Advanced.

skills.skill: Cold Plate and Coolant Loop Assembly
skills.why: Current server racks are liquid cooled; the loop is assembled and leak-tested on the line.

careers.title: Consumer Electronics Assembler
careers.basis: A high-volume device line: the five device skills the catalogue has, with the station's test. The catalogue note lists them.

careers.title: Wafer Fab Operator
careers.basis: The cleanroom foundation and the lot run by the system: gown, handle wafers, run the recipe called for, log it, flag what is out of control. O*NET 51-9141 tasks and tools (clean room suits, wafer handling, cleaning) and the federal apprenticeship framework for Semiconductor Processing Technician ("follows all cleanroom environment protocols", "interprets information from process control charts"); the module skills now sit in the five process technician careers, as the catalogue note says.

careers.title: Lithography Process Technician
careers.basis: The photo module: track, scanner and the three checks that keep a pattern in specification. The operator's foundation is kept whole; EUV is the Advanced end, as the catalogue note says.

skills.why: A wafer that fails inspection after develop is stripped and reworked in the photo area.

careers.title: Etch Process Technician
careers.basis: The etch module: the two plasma processes and the ash strip, the vacuum and gas knowledge a chamber needs, and the etch-rate, particle and dimension monitors that requalify it after maintenance.

skills.why: Etch rate is monitored by film thickness before and after.
A chamber is leak-checked before it is returned to production.

careers.title: Thin Film Process Technician
careers.basis: Four draft paths meet here; a technician is hired into one deposition method and rotates through the rest, so the path names them all and the three film monitors (thickness, stress, sheet resistance). From the catalogue note and O*NET 51-9141 tools (CVD, LPCVD, PECVD and PVD systems, epitaxial deposition equipment).

careers.title: Diffusion and Implant Process Technician
careers.basis: Furnaces, rapid thermal tools and implanters, with the thickness and sheet-resistance monitors that prove them.

skills.why: An implanter is a high-voltage accelerator; its technicians are trained for it before anything else.
Furnace nitride and polysilicon run in the diffusion area.

careers.title: Wet Process and CMP Technician
careers.basis: Two modules in one career, as the catalogue note explains: baths and their chemistry, the polisher, and the rate and defect monitors.

careers.title: Semiconductor Metrology Technician
careers.basis: Every in-line measurement and the review of what inspection finds: the catalogue's wafer metrology and defect groups. The nine folded titles are single instruments.

careers.title: Semiconductor Equipment Technician
careers.basis: Intel's manufacturing equipment technician posting, read in full: preventive and corrective maintenance in a cleanroom, wet chemistry and high-vacuum toolsets, electrical schematics and mechanical drawings, multimeter and oscilloscope. Micron's fab equipment technician posting says the same in fewer words. Neither names a tool vendor: makes are the leaf beyond these skills.

skills.why: A tool is requalified with monitor wafers after maintenance.

lacks: RF generator and matching network service

careers.title: Semiconductor Equipment Engineer
careers.basis: Owns the fleet the technician maintains: the same equipment skills, read through availability data, sensor traces and root cause. Five draft paths met here and shared exactly these; Texas Instruments' equipment engineer posting names the reactors by make, which is a company's version of this path.

careers.title: Lithography Process Engineer
careers.basis: The technician's module with the engineer's method: process windows from focus-exposure data, overlay and dimension control by experiment and capability, and the mask corrections the computational titles bring.

careers.title: Etch Process Engineer
careers.basis: The etch module with the experiments that widen its window and the trace monitoring that matches chambers.

careers.title: Thin Film Process Engineer
careers.basis: The deposition methods and film monitors of the technician path, owned as recipes and film properties.

careers.title: Diffusion and Implant Process Engineer
careers.basis: Thermal and doping processes with the measurements that show the junction and the film they made.

skills.why: A dopant profile is read from SIMS; the implant engineer specifies and interprets it.

careers.title: Wet Process and CMP Engineer
careers.basis: Cleans, wet etch and polish owned as chemistries, removal rates and defects.

careers.title: Process Integration Engineer
careers.basis: One working skill from each module, because integration is how the modules fit: then electrical results, maps and experiments. Six careers lead here and each finds its own module on the path.

careers.title: Yield Engineer
careers.basis: Wafer maps, inline defect data and electrical test traced to a tool or a step. The metrology technician's defect skills are kept; the rest is analysis.

careers.title: Failure Analysis Technician
careers.basis: The laboratory's instruments, one skill each, as the catalogue note lists them. Short because the catalogue has no skill for half the instruments the folded titles name.

skills.why: Decapsulation and delayering are wet etches.

lacks: package decapsulation as its own skill

careers.title: Failure Analysis Engineer
careers.basis: Directs the analysis the technician carries out: isolates the fault electrically first, names the mechanism, writes the corrective action.

careers.title: Semiconductor Packaging Technician
careers.basis: One back-end line: dice, attach, bond, underfill, mold, mark, with the pull and shear tests. The catalogue note says its packaging skills make one full path; they do.

careers.title: Semiconductor Packaging Engineer
careers.basis: The assembly process owned and qualified: the line's steps, their reliability under stress, and the engineering statistics.
lacks: thermal and mechanical simulation of a package

careers.title: Semiconductor Test Technician
careers.basis: Probe and final test: prober, handler and tester set up, the program loaded, the cell kept yielding.

careers.title: Semiconductor Test Engineer
careers.basis: Writes the test programs the technician runs and proves the testers agree: coverage, limits, correlation.

skills.why: Tester-to-tester correlation is a measurement system study.

careers.title: Battery Electrode Technician
careers.basis: Mix, coat, calender, slit, with loading and thickness controlled along the way. The draft path of Electrode Coating Technician and the two skills the catalogue note brings; no electrode posting was among those read.

skills.why: Cathode slurry is made with a regulated solvent and toxic metal oxide powders.

careers.title: Battery Cell Assembly Technician
careers.basis: Wound or stacked, the cell assembly line step by step: the catalogue's cell assembly group, with notching and stacking added last round. Panasonic's cell plant posts its technicians by station (Winding, Top Cap): of 39 station-technician postings read (29 of them Panasonic's), 37 ask machine operation, all keep records, 29 inspect, 28 troubleshoot and 25 name protective equipment; none names a process skill.

skills.why: Every wound or stacked cell is checked for an internal short before filling.

careers.title: Battery Cell Formation Technician
careers.basis: Formation cycling, degas, aging and grading: the catalogue's cell finishing group is this career.

careers.title: Battery Pack Assembly Technician
careers.basis: Cells to modules to a sealed, tested pack: three draft paths (pack, module, busbar welding) are one line, and the ten folded titles are its stations.

careers.title: Battery Cell Engineer
careers.basis: The whole cell line known step by step, since three technician careers lead here, and the engineering method that shows a change is better. From the career description and the present path; the cell engineer postings read are almost all for solar and satellite cells and were not used.
lacks: electrochemical test (cycling, impedance) as a skill

careers.title: Battery Pack Engineer
careers.basis: A mechanical designer's path with the two tests a pack design is proven by. The catalogue describes how a pack is built and tested, not how one is designed, so the design side is the general engineering skills.
lacks: high-voltage architecture, isolation and creepage design

careers.title: Electric Motor Assembler
careers.basis: Stator, rotor, then the motor in its housing: the catalogue's electric motor build group, with the balance, the fits and the winding tests. The draft path of Hairpin Stator Technician and the skills the catalogue note brings.

skills.why: Hairpin ends are laser welded.

careers.title: Food Processing Operator
careers.basis: Food safety first, then the batch and the thermal step. The catalogue note lists the path; O*NET 51-3092 tasks (mix or blend ingredients to recipes) and 51-3093 (cook to time and temperature, clean and sterilize equipment). No food maker's postings were read. Nothing in the catalogue is Advanced for it.

careers.title: Beverage Production Operator
careers.basis: Syrup room to palletizer: blend, carbonate, fill, seam or cap, with the bottle blown on the same line. The catalogue note lists the path; blow molding was added last round.

skills.why: The syrup room; Brix measurement is now part of this skill.

careers.title: Packaging Line Operator
careers.basis: End-of-line machines kept fed and running, changed over between sizes, with codes and weights checked. O*NET 51-9111 tasks (clear jams, attach labels, check and adjust weights); the lot and GMP skills are what the pharmaceutical titles folded here add.

careers.title: Chemical Operator
careers.basis: Outside operator to board operator: transfers, charging, the reactor and the column, then the control room. O*NET 51-9011 tasks and tools (reactors, distillers, charging by valve and pump) and 51-8091 (control boards, sampling); no chemical maker's postings were read.

skills.why: Vessels are entered for cleaning and inspection under permit.

careers.title: Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Operator
careers.basis: Dispense, blend, granulate, compress, coat, every step in the batch record. The catalogue note lists the path; weighing and dispensing was added last round. Process validation is the engineer's and is left off.

careers.title: Aseptic Filling Technician
careers.basis: Gowned to qualification, the line set up aseptically, filled, freeze-dried and monitored: the catalogue's aseptic processing group.

skills.why: Filling parts and stoppers are autoclaved by the line's own technicians.

careers.title: Sterilization Technician
careers.basis: Two sterilizers, the validated load pattern and the records that release a cycle. Short: the catalogue has two skills for the trade.

skills.why: Ethylene oxide is toxic and flammable.

careers.title: Quality Control Chemist
careers.basis: The laboratory's four methods and the release decision. Short and honest: the catalogue note lists these and no more.

careers.title: Quality Control Microbiologist
careers.basis: Bioburden, endotoxin and sterility, with the room monitoring behind them. Short for the same reason as the chemist.

careers.title: Process Engineer
careers.basis: Rewritten as the catalogue note asks: the process read from its P&ID and its data, its variation studied, each change validated. The unit operations are the ones the catalogue has (reactor, column, extruder, molding).

skills.why: A plastics plant's process engineer owns the extrusion line; no career in the catalogue runs one.
The plastics version of process development, added last round for this career.

careers.title: Quality Control Inspector
careers.basis: The bench inspector at any point in the flow. Of 59 quality inspector postings read (SpaceX 19, Panasonic 12, Rocket Lab 9, Anduril 7), 53 name the plant system, 41 nonconformance write-ups, 32 calipers or micrometers, 30 first article, 26 visual or workmanship inspection, 25 GD&T, 22 a CMM and 17 receiving inspection; O*NET lists the gauges. Gauge studies and auditing are the engineer's and are taken off.

skills.why: An inspector checks assemblies as well as parts; it is also what an assembler brings to this job.

careers.title: CMM Programmer
careers.basis: One career from running programs to writing them, as the catalogue note says: the inspector's drawing and bench skills, then alignment to datums and the program from the model. Of 11 CMM and metrology postings read, all name GD&T and programming and 9 a CMM software make.

skills.why: Programs are written offline from the CAD model.

careers.title: Dimensional Metrology Technician
careers.basis: Large and freeform measurement: tracker, scanner and arm, aligned to datums, turned into a report by zone. The draft path of Body Dimensional Inspector with the two skills the catalogue note adds.

careers.title: Calibration Technician
careers.basis: The calibration skills kept and the CMM work taken off, as the catalogue note asks: every kind of instrument a plant sends to its laboratory, the standards it is compared with, and the uncertainty of the result.

careers.title: Metrology Engineer
careers.basis: Decides how a product is measured and proves the measurement: the methods of the three careers that lead here, with capability, gauge studies and uncertainty.

careers.title: Aircraft Assembly Inspector
careers.basis: A mechanic who now buys off the work: fastener, sealant and safety workmanship, closeout of each zone, and the records that make the aircraft conform. The path is the catalogue note's; 38 of 59 quality inspector postings speak of mechanics' or assembly work, which is why the mechanic's skills are kept under the inspector's.

skills.why: Kept from the mechanic's path: an inspector accepts sealant and safety wire only by knowing how they are done.
The airworthiness side of the job: the conformity record is the inspector's signature.

careers.title: Vehicle Final Inspector
careers.basis: End of line: the catalogue's vehicle end-of-line testing group, with fit and finish. Nothing in it is Advanced.

skills.why: A failed end-of-line check is read from the vehicle's fault codes first.

careers.title: Quality Engineer
careers.basis: Quality built in and escapes closed out. Of 99 quality engineer postings read, 96 name corrective action, 84 root cause, 76 first article, 65 FMEA, 55 audits, 55 GD&T, 54 PPAP or APQP, 53 capability, 45 the material review board, 36 control plans, 35 gauge studies and 31 SPC.

careers.title: NDT Technician (Penetrant)
careers.basis: The first method most inspectors certify in. Three method skills after last round's folding, completed from visual testing and the record, as the catalogue report advises.

skills.why: Most penetrant work is on welds, and a weld is looked at before it is processed.

careers.title: NDT Technician (Magnetic Particle)
careers.basis: The second surface method, added to the first: a technician certified in both is the usual case, and the penetrant skills are kept.

careers.title: NDT Technician
careers.basis: The multi-method technician: the two surface methods kept, one working skill from each volumetric method added. Of 23 NDT postings read (SpaceX 13, Relativity 8), 20 or more name each of penetrant, ultrasonic, radiographic, eddy current and visual testing, 22 certification to NAS 410 or SNT-TC-1A, and 12 digital radiography or CT; leak testing is the folded title.

careers.title: NDT Technician (Ultrasonic)
careers.basis: Levels I to III and four techniques in one career, as the catalogue note says: calibrate, scan by contact, angle and immersion, size, then phased array and time-of-flight, then the procedure and the reference standard.

careers.title: NDT Technician (Radiographic)
careers.basis: Film, digital, real-time and CT, with the safety and the interpretation: the catalogue's radiographic group.

careers.title: NDT Technician (Eddy Current)
careers.basis: The catalogue's eddy current group whole, completed from the visual methods and the record.
skills: Eddy Current Inspection of Aircraft Structure

careers.title: NDT Technician (Composites)
careers.basis: An ultrasonic technician on composite and bonded structure: the ultrasonic skills kept, then the methods bonded structure needs. The draft path of NDI Composite Inspector with the three the catalogue note brings.

skills.why: The folded title Thermography Inspector; the catalogue files the skill under maintenance.

careers.title: Test Technician
careers.basis: Set up, run, record, diagnose. Of 53 test technician postings read (SpaceX, Anduril, Rocket Lab, Applied Materials), 38 name troubleshooting, 30 data acquisition, 19 schematics and 16 environmental test; many are fluid-system test, which is the propulsion test technician's. The six careers that lead here bring the product, and this path is what they add.

skills.why: The spacecraft branch the catalogue note names.
The high-voltage branch: what a tester from an inverter or battery line specialises in.

careers.title: RF Technician
careers.basis: An electronics or test technician who has taken up the two RF instruments: build and tune the hardware, then measure it on a network and a spectrum analyzer. The catalogue note lists the path.

careers.title: Powertrain Test Technician
careers.basis: The unit bolted to the stand, connected, run through its cycle and read. The catalogue note lists the path; data acquisition was added last round.

skills.why: Noise and vibration signatures are how an end-of-line stand finds a bad gear or bearing.

careers.title: Propulsion Test Technician
careers.basis: A test stand is a fluid system with an engine on it: the build technician's fitting, leak-check and inspection skills, the stand's instrumentation, then loading and firing. Seven test stand technician postings carried the title (SpaceX 4, Relativity 3): all name fittings and tubing, 6 instrumentation, 6 pressure systems, 4 cryogenics and 4 data acquisition. Rocket and jet test in one career, as the catalogue note says.

skills.why: A stand is built and operated from its fluid schematic. No technician posting names it (83 of 124 propulsion engineer postings do); my judgment.

careers.title: Launch Pad Technician
careers.basis: Ground systems: lifting and work at height, the fluid and hydraulic systems of the pad, umbilicals and quick-disconnects, then loading. Of 11 launch and ground systems technician postings read (Relativity 4, Rocket Lab 4, SpaceX 3), all name fluid, cryogenic or propellant systems and 9 cranes, lifts or rigging.

careers.title: Test Engineer
careers.basis: The technician's bench skills kept, then the engineer's own. Of 197 test engineer postings read (Anduril 86, SpaceX 53), 188 name requirements or verification, 135 test procedures or plans, 133 Python, 126 automation, 109 vibration or environmental test, 96 data acquisition, 86 CAN, 69 hardware in the loop and 46 EMC.

careers.title: Product Reliability Engineer
careers.basis: Stress, burn-in and accelerated life tests designed and read, and the failure fed back to design. Takes the draft path of Semiconductor Reliability Engineer, widened from chips to products.

careers.title: Maintenance Technician
careers.basis: The multi-craft mechanic. Of 42 maintenance technician postings read (SpaceX 21, Panasonic 5, Anduril 4, Lucid 3, Rivian 3), 38 name electrical work and troubleshooting, 32 schematics or drawings, 31 pneumatics, 28 hydraulics, 22 motors, 21 a maintenance system or work orders, 21 bearings, gears or alignment, 20 PLCs and 17 preventive maintenance. The federal Industrial Equipment Mechanic standard (grade 10: "lay out, install, align, repair, overhaul") and O*NET 49-9041 give the mechanical side.

skills.why: Going online to find the fault, not writing the program: that is the controls technician.

careers.title: Millwright
careers.basis: Move it, set it, align it, rebuild it. O*NET 49-9044 tasks ("align machines or equipment, using hoists, jacks, hand tools, squares, rules, micrometers") and tools (levels, alignment telescopes, welders); six postings carried the title.

careers.title: Industrial Electrician
careers.basis: Plant power to the motor terminals: distribution, conduit and wire, motors and their controls, tested and troubleshot live. O*NET 47-2111 tasks and tools (conduit benders, circuit testers). Of 18 electrician postings read (SpaceX 12), all name schematics or drawings, 8 high or medium voltage, 6 motor controls and 6 drives.

careers.title: Hydraulics Technician
careers.basis: The catalogue's fluid power group, on the machine and on the bench, with the tube and fitting skills added last round.

careers.title: Reliability Engineer
careers.basis: Plant equipment reliability, as the catalogue note settles it: breakdown history from the maintenance system, the condition-monitoring methods, the strategy, and root cause on chronic failures. Leans Advanced because the catalogue's reliability methods are.

skills.why: The failure-mode analysis behind a maintenance strategy; the catalogue has no separate equipment FMEA.

careers.title: Facilities Engineer
careers.basis: A plant's utilities, each one a catalogue skill: power, air, cooling, water, gases and chemicals, and their reliability. Of 17 facilities engineer postings read, 12 name electrical power, 12 building controls, 9 HVAC or chilled water, 7 AutoCAD and 6 water systems.

careers.title: Aircraft Mechanic
careers.basis: Certificated maintenance: the manuals first, then airframe, systems and engine work signed for. The federal Aircraft Mechanic standard (grade 10: "install, adjust, align, troubleshoot and perform final functional and operational tests" on major systems) and the present path, with the build-line skills of the systems mechanic kept under it.

careers.title: Aircraft Engine Mechanic
careers.basis: Teardown, inspect, rebuild, balance, run. The catalogue note lists the path; the mechanic's manual, tool-control and record skills are kept.
lacks: fuel nozzle and accessory bench test

careers.title: Automation Technician
careers.basis: A maintenance technician whose machines are automated cells: the electrical and pneumatic skills kept, then robots, sensing, vision and the network. Of 21 controls, instrumentation and automation technician postings read (one set for this career and the controls technician), 16 name troubleshooting, 14 schematics, 13 drives or servos, 12 sensors, 10 vision and 8 pneumatics.

careers.title: Controls Technician
careers.basis: Goes online with the PLC, tunes drives and loops, calibrates instruments, fixes the network. Of 21 controls, instrumentation and automation technician postings read (SpaceX 13, Panasonic 4), 15 name instrumentation or calibration, 13 drives or servos, 12 sensors, 7 PLCs and 6 networks. Four careers lead here and each keeps its electrical foundation.

careers.title: Robotics Technician
careers.basis: Install, master, recover, maintain. Robot mastering was added last round for this career; collaborative robots are the folded title Cobot Technician.

careers.title: Robot Programmer
careers.basis: Programs at the pendant and offline, for the processes robots carry: welding, handling, painting. The technician's robot skills are kept; simulation is the Advanced end.

skills.why: A weld path is programmed by someone who can read the weld; it is also what a robotic welding technician brings.
The folded title Paint Robot Programmer.

careers.title: Controls Engineer
careers.basis: Designs what the controls technician maintains. Of 69 controls engineer postings read (SpaceX 27, Anduril 17), 53 name PLCs, 46 commissioning, 46 vision, 43 robots, 41 motion or servos, 41 SCADA, 38 industrial networks, 37 electrical design, 30 HMIs, 29 PID control and 20 safety systems.

skills.why: Robots are named in 43 of 69 controls engineer postings: the controls engineer integrates and often programs them.
Named in 46 of 69 postings.

careers.title: Automation Engineer
careers.basis: The cell designed and integrated. Of 23 automation engineer postings read (Anduril 13, SpaceX 7), 22 name vision, 22 cells or integration, 20 robots, 19 safety, 17 PLCs, 17 CAD or mechanical design, 12 Python and 9 end-of-arm tooling. Vision folds here because the catalogue has two vision skills.

skills.why: Commissioning is done at the pendant; it is also what the technician brings.

careers.title: Manufacturing Engineer
careers.basis: How the product is built. Of 239 manufacturing engineer postings read, 171 name design for manufacture, 147 tooling or fixtures, 132 the MES or ERP, 119 work instructions and 79 root cause.

careers.title: Mechanical Engineer
careers.basis: The designer's CAD and tolerancing, then sizing by analysis and the plan that verifies the design. Of 270 mechanical engineer postings read (Anduril 84, SpaceX 84), 224 name requirements, 223 CAD, 153 finite element analysis, 142 drawings, 114 GD&T, 99 design for manufacture, 85 PLM and 61 tolerance analysis.

careers.title: Electrical Engineer
careers.basis: Circuit to board to proof. Of 183 electrical engineer postings read (Anduril 70, SpaceX 60), 146 name requirements, 139 verification or validation, 134 PCB layout, 125 schematics, 98 bring-up or debug, 92 CAN, 87 lab instruments and 65 EMC.

skills.why: Named in 92 of 183 postings.
The equipment side of the career (wiring and controls), added to the catalogue for it; few product postings name it.

careers.title: Tooling Engineer
careers.basis: Designs the tooling and proves it on the floor. Of 14 tooling engineer postings read (SpaceX 5, Anduril 4), 13 name CAD, 12 tool design, 12 analysis, 12 machining or fabrication knowledge and 9 GD&T. The toolroom hand skills on the present path (grinding, EDM) are the toolmaker's and are taken off.

skills.why: Tooling is designed for the changeover: locating, clamping and connections standardised.

careers.title: CAD Designer
careers.basis: Models, drawings and their revisions: the catalogue's CAD and drawings group, with the tolerancing a detail drawing needs. Short because the job is: five near-identical drafting titles fold here.

skills.why: The folded title Electrical Drafter; the catalogue has no skill for drawing schematics below the engineer's.

careers.title: Systems Engineer
careers.basis: Requirements down, verification up: the two systems skills added last round, with the test and risk skills that carry them. Short because the catalogue still has no skill for interfaces or architecture.
lacks: system architecture and model-based systems engineering

careers.title: Aerospace Engineer
careers.basis: Structures design and its support of the build. Of 61 structures and stress engineer postings read, 49 name requirements, 48 finite element analysis, 42 CAD, 36 loads, 27 drawings and 26 fatigue or damage tolerance; the disposition of nonconforming hardware is named by 5 and is here from the career description.

careers.title: Propulsion Engineer
careers.basis: A design engineer who proves the design on the stand. Of 124 propulsion engineer postings read (SpaceX 48, Rocket Lab 29, Relativity 22), 118 name test, 116 design, 102 requirements, 83 fluid systems or P&IDs, 80 CAD, 48 instrumentation and 44 test procedures.

careers.title: Automotive Engineer
careers.basis: The general design path, with the vehicle's network. The catalogue cannot tell body, chassis, powertrain and NVH engineers apart, as its note says.

careers.title: Biomedical Engineer
careers.basis: Device design under a quality system: the design path, then risk analysis, verification and validation and the audit it must survive. The catalogue note lists the path.
lacks: design controls and the design history file
